Annual Report & Financial Statements 2015

2015
Highlights
CIRCULAR ECONOMY
The cement sector is an energy intensive sector in the region. Providing sustainable solutions to reduce our dependency on natural
resources and fossil fuels, as well as energy conservation is a high priority for the Group.
Coffee Development Project
The Hima Coffee Development Project was born out of the need to secure sustainable access to renewable energy while benefitting
local coffee producing communities towards poverty alleviation and economic growth. Our operations in Uganda have made enormous
Our
achievements on use of biomass as an alternative fuel (AF), with an above 50% substitution ratio. The biomass is sourced from local
Business communities in Uganda and northern Tanzania. The streams of biomass used include; coffee husks, rice husks, palm kernels and
sugar bagasse. Coffee husks forms the highest component of the alternative fuel accounting for up to 50% of the total Alternative Fuel.
Coffee is produced in large quantities in Uganda and represents more than 50% of exports. Large volumes of coffee husks traditionally
dumped now being used as fuel. To ensure continuity of the biomass supply, especially coffee husks, Hima Cement Uganda embarked
on the “Coffee Project” which aim is to supply coffee seedlings to the local farmers and offer agricultural extension services through
partnership with local associations. The maturity of coffee bushes is three (3) years. Three farmers’ associations are involved in the
implementation and with partners including Local Government Authorities, whose role is to mobilize farmers and to provide agricultural
extension services. The Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) provides certified coffee seeds required for the project and
Operational offer training. The project covers the following coffee production processes: Coffee seedling production and distribution, Coffee
development, Coffee agricultural extension services with the objective to substantially increase coffee production in Kasese /Kamwenge
districts, raise living standards by increasing household incomes.
